rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for the offer! I'm excited to have your help. I've been moving quickly on Halcyon Threshold since the meetup and would really value your 5 hours a week. Here's what I've built so far: - Website: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app - GitHub repo with initial content (research syntheses, neglected areas analysis, resources) - Grant proposal to Emberfall Fund (applying by Nov 30) What would help most right now: 1. **Fact-checking and review** (2-3 hrs/week): Review my research syntheses for technical accuracy. You'd read drafts, verify claims, check citations, and flag anything that seems wrong or overstated. 2. **Literature review** (2-3 hrs/week): Help me identify important papers/work for upcoming syntheses. I'm planning pieces on interpretability progress, deception research, and AI governance - finding the key sources would be hugely helpful. Does this sound like a good use of your time? I can be flexible on the specific breakdown, and we can adjust as we figure out what works. I'm planning to meet weekly (maybe Sunday afternoons?) to coordinate, and we can use a shared Google Doc for async collaboration. Let me know what you think! Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Responded positively to her offer of 5 hrs/week help with specific tasks (fact-checking, literature review). Awaiting her response.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Application: Research Synthesis and Coordination Infrastructure". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks again for the conversation at the meetup. I'm submitting a rapid grant application for Halcyon Threshold. **Project**: Research synthesis and coordination infrastructure for the AI safety ecosystem **Amount**: $18,000 **Duration**: 4 months (Dec 2026 - Mar 2027) I've attached a 2-page proposal below. The short version: I'll produce 10-12 research syntheses, a systematic \"neglected areas map,\" and practical resources for independent researchers and funders. Work samples are available now: - Website: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app - GitHub: github.com/halcyon-threshold (see research/, neglected-areas/, resources/) - Three substantial pieces already complete I've been working evenings and weekends on this for the past month, and I have one collaborator (Priya Raman, data analyst) who's volunteered 5 hrs/week. The grant would let us scale up and produce more systematic output. Happy to answer any questions or provide additional information. Best, Morgan --- # PROPOSAL: RESEARCH SYNTHESIS AND COORDINATION INFRASTRUCTURE **Applicant**: Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold **Amount**: $18,000 over 4 months **Contact**: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org ## What We'll Do Produce high-quality research syntheses and coordination infrastructure: 1. **Research Syntheses** (10-12 pieces): Clear, accurate summaries of important AI safety research for specific audiences (funders, policymakers, researchers in adjacent areas, newcomers). Topics include evaluation methodologies, interpretability progress, deception research, governance approaches, and emerging risk categories. 2,000-4,000 words each, technically accurate, expert-reviewed. 2. **Neglected Areas Map** (10-15 analyses): Systematic identification of under-resourced research areas with evidence of importance, neglect, and tractability. Concrete next steps for each. Updated monthly. 3. **Practical Resources** (3-4 guides): Independent researcher guide (complete), grant opportunity tracker, funder's guide to evaluation quality, collaboration templates. 4. **Infrastructure**: Public website, monthly newsletter, office hours for community questions. **Value Proposition**: The field consistently cites lack of good synthesis as a bottleneck. We fill this gap, making coordination failures visible and helping everyone work more effectively. ## Why Me - 5 years professional technical writing (B2B software at Dorrance) - Python and data analysis skills - Deep AI safety literature engagement (2 years) - Already have collaborator (Priya Raman, 5 hrs/week volunteer) - Already started: 3 substantial pieces complete (see halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app) - Independent status allows radical honesty without organizational constraints ## Budget: $18,000 **Compensation** ($16,400 - adjusted to $16,000 to fit budget): - My time: 20 hrs/week × 16 weeks @ $45/hr = $14,400 (below day job rate but sustainable) - Priya Raman: 5 hrs/week × 16 weeks @ $50/hr = $4,000 (data analysis, literature review, fact-checking) - Adjusted to $16,000 total compensation **Operating** ($2,000): - Domain/hosting: $95 - Research subscriptions: $300 - Expert consultation: $500 - Newsletter infrastructure: $100 - Contingency: $1,005 ## Success Metrics **Outputs**: 10+ syntheses, 10+ neglected areas, 3+ guides, website live **Impact**: Content cited by researchers/funders, neglected areas get attention, positive expert feedback, 100+ newsletter subscribers **Process**: All work public, monthly updates, quick error correction ## Timeline - **Month 1**: 3 syntheses, 4 neglected areas, website complete - **Month 2**: 3 more syntheses, 4 more neglected areas, 2 guides - **Month 3**: 2 more syntheses, 2 more neglected areas, remaining guides - **Month 4**: 2 final syntheses, update all content, impact report ## Risk Mitigation - Getting feedback early to validate value - Expert review for technical accuracy - Conservative scope (proven I can work part-time) - Explicit uncertainty notation - Willing to pivot if learning synthesis isn't valuable --- **Work samples**: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app - Research synthesis: AI Safety Evaluations methodological overview - Neglected area: Open Source AI Safety - Resource: Independent Researcher Guide"
rows.quote: Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant: $18,000 for 4 months submitted to Idris Bellamy by Nov 30 deadline.
